title: Titanium Coilover Spring
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) offers the best balance of high strength (yield >830 MPa), excellent fatigue resistance, and corrosion resistance for precision-machined components. Its strength-to-weight ratio is 45% better than steel, making it the most widely used titanium alloy in aerospace, medical, and industrial applications.
commonFailures: Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86)

faq.q: What is a titanium coilover spring?
faq.a: A titanium coilover spring is a precision-machined suspension component used in high-performance racing coil suspension spring (beta-c). Manufactured from Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What is the typical application for titanium coilover spring?
faq.a: Titanium Coilover Spring is designed for high-performance racing coil suspension spring (beta-c). The Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V grade is selected to provide the optimal balance of strength, fatigue life, and environmental resistance for this specific application.

faq.q: How is titanium coilover spring manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Coilover Spring is manufactured using Hot forging. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium coilover spring?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.
